source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: Royal Enfield international revenue rose to about Rs 3,288 cr in FY26 from Rs 2,546 cr in FY25, and international volumes grew about 20% to 120,634 units. The company is diversifying through CKD assembly (a second Brazil plant, a Mexico plant under evaluation), but there is no explicit China+1 narrative.

crude_exposure.evidence: Commentary on FY26 quarters cites rising raw material prices squeezing Royal Enfield margins. No crude-linked share was disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Proxy only: Rs 3,288 cr of international revenue against about Rs 23,408 cr of FY26 consolidated revenue is roughly 14% (my own calculation). Management said international business was about 15% of revenue in Q1 FY27. No hedging policy was found in search results.

pli_scheme.evidence: The Ministry of Heavy Industries lists Eicher Motors Ltd among approved applicants under the PLI-Auto Champion OEM Incentive scheme (except 2W/3W category; it covers BEV and hydrogen vehicles). No incentive amount was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: The FY26 AR says Uno Minda is building customer relationships across Europe, North America and SE Asia. It has plants in Indonesia, Vietnam and Mexico, and management expects exports to become a 'meaningfully larger' share of revenue over 3-5 years. Its localisation and import-substitution push is not framed explicitly as China+1.

inr_exposure.evidence: Proxy is the export share of turnover, 4% per the BRSR filed July 2026 (likely FY26). That BRSR basis probably excludes revenue of overseas subsidiaries, so consolidated international exposure is likely somewhat higher. No hedging policy was found.

pli_scheme.evidence: The approved PLI-Auto applicant list (as of 30.11.2025) includes the Uno Minda group as Component Champion via Denso Ten Uno Minda India. A company filing says telematics, BCMs, VCUs, sensors and select CNG components qualify. Q1 FY26 revenue included about Rs 69 cr of prior-period incentive income, but the scheme was not named.

china_plus_one.evidence: Hotel operator with an international portfolio (US, UK, Dubai, Maldives, Sri Lanka, Cape Town). No export or supply-chain narrative.

inr_exposure.evidence: Proxy is the international business share. A May 2025 trade-press report (FY25 basis) put international owned and managed hotels at about 20% of consolidated revenue, with the two US hotels at about 10%. In FY26 the West Asia conflict reportedly cut international revenue by an estimated 5-7%, and Dubai occupancy fell to about 25%, while London stayed stable.

china_plus_one.evidence: International revenue dominates: North America was 48% of FY26 revenue (+53% reported, about +9% normalised for US tariff effects) and Europe grew 34%, with a GBP 100 mn Europe revenue target by 2030. Basmati is origin-specific, so there is no China+1 or supply-chain diversification angle.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Reported to hedge currency exposure generally (per older earnings-call commentary relayed in an investor forum). No formal policy was found.
inr_exposure.evidence: Proxy is the international share. India was about 29% of revenue in 9M FY26 and North America (US+Canada, used here as the US field) was 48% in FY26, so non-India revenue is about 71%. That mixes a 9M basis with a full-year basis.

pli_scheme.evidence: No confirmation of PLI (food processing) approval was found in search results.

china_plus_one.evidence: Exports are 7.01% of turnover per the BRSR (filed July 2026). US exports weakened after the India-US tariff revision (Q3 FY26 exports -13.5%), and management expects a rebound. International subsidiaries grew 6.1% in FY26. No diversification narrative.

rural.evidence: Management said rural growth continued to outpace urban for several quarters in FY26, and brokers cite rurban and semi-urban volume recovery. No rural revenue share was disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: VAM, a crude derivative, was historically cited as 35-40% of raw material costs (Business Standard, 2019; dated). Around Q4 FY26 the West Asia crisis drove about 40-50% raw material basket inflation, with VAM more than doubling to about $1,800/t, and Pidilite took price hikes of about 9-15%.

inr_exposure.evidence: Proxy is the BRSR export share of 7.01% of turnover. That excludes revenue of overseas subsidiaries in Asia and the Middle East & Africa (FY25: Asia Rs 323 cr, MEA Rs 309 cr), so total foreign-currency revenue is likely somewhat higher. No hedging policy was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: FY26 export dispatches rose ~40% YoY to 4,02,786 units (vs 2,87,429 in FY25), presence in 52 countries incl. new Europe/UK entries (Germany as 53rd in Jul-2026); growth attributed to an '80-20' focus on top-10 markets, not a China+1/supply-chain angle. Export revenue share not disclosed; exports were ~6% of FY26 total volumes (~64.7 lakh units).

rural.evidence: No FY26 rural revenue share disclosed; coverage cites Hero's deep rural dealer network and brand recall as a structural advantage, with rural recovery named as a volume driver.

crude_exposure.evidence: Management named aluminium, steel, rubber and plastics as key inflationary commodities, with plastics hit by elevated crude prices; Q4 FY26 commodity cost rose ~Rs 2.1k/unit vs ~Rs 2.0k/unit price increase (brokerage note).

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue not separately disclosed (exports ~6% of FY26 volumes). A brokerage noted ~25bps margin benefit from forex in Q4 FY26; no formal hedging policy found in search.

pli_scheme.evidence: Hero's VIDA V2 Pro electric scooter was cleared by testing agencies (8 Jul 2025) under the Rs 25,938 cr PLI-Auto scheme, making Hero the fourth e-2W maker in the PLI roster (Mint, Jul 2025). Incentive amounts not disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Domestic retailer; international footprint limited to 6 Zudio stores in UAE out of 1,286 total stores at 31-Mar-2026. No export business.

rural.evidence: No rural split disclosed. Per Tata group newsroom, ~900 of 1,286 stores are in tier-2 to tier-4 markets, contributing ~63% of FY26 revenue (non-metro revenue grew ~25%); Zudio added 78 new cities in FY26 (310 cities). Not a rural metric.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Trent was net cash at end-FY26 (brokerage note). FY26 consolidated finance cost ~Rs 168 cr, largely Ind AS 116 lease interest; no floating-rate debt split found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Revenue essentially INR-denominated (FY26 standalone revenue Rs 19,701 cr); only 6 UAE stores abroad.

china_plus_one.evidence: FY26 exports were a record, ~9-10% of revenue and 5-6% of volume per Outlook Business (another outlet says ~8%); Africa, APAC and airport retail offset Middle East disruption (no shipments to Gulf in Mar-Apr 2026). No supply-chain diversification angle.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Net debt reduced by Rs 329 cr in FY26; management targets net debt-free status in FY27. Floating-rate mix not disclosed in search results.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key inputs are grain/ENA and glass, not crude derivatives; raw materials added ~225bps gross margin in Q4 FY26, while glass prices rose ~15-20% in 2026 (CARE Ratings, sell-side notes).

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Board risk management policy covers INR risk on import, export and loan exposures; speculative currency activity is prohibited.
inr_exposure.evidence: Export share (~9-10% of FY26 revenue, secondary estimate) used as proxy for foreign-currency revenue.

china_plus_one.evidence: FY26 revenue Rs 3,314 cr (+41%) was export-driven: CDMO +59% (exports >96% of segment), specialty chem +44%, HPP +34%; HFO supply contract with Solstice extended to Dec-2032. China+1 framing comes from analysts (new 15,000 tpa R32 capacity) rather than explicit company attribution.

rate_sensitive.evidence: CARE Ratings (Aug-2026) says the company was net debt-free at 31-Mar-2026 (net debt/PBILDT -0.05x vs 1.79x in FY25); FY26 interest paid ~Rs 106 cr (aggregator). Floating-rate share not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY26 export revenue Rs 2,225.4 cr vs domestic Rs 1,088.5 cr (~67% exports), used as foreign-currency revenue proxy; CARE flags forex, tariff and geopolitical risk from sizeable exports. Hedging policy not found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: A USD 550mn dollar-denominated loan raised in India (Q4 FY26 brokerage note) acts as a natural currency hedge; rate type not disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Cash-flow hedges on forex receivables; from FY26 realized hedge gains/losses are reclassified from revenue to other income. The USD 550mn loan serves as a natural hedge, and the open hedge book runs off by Q3 FY27.
inr_exposure.evidence: FY26 revenue USD 1,870mn (Rs 16,403 cr): Americas 56.9% (Rs 9,334 cr), EMEA 28.9%, RoW 14.2% (RoW includes India, which is not split out). Americas share is used as the USD-revenue proxy. Q1 FY27 hedge loss was USD 10mn plus USD 14mn MTM on outstanding hedges.

china_plus_one.evidence: FY26 exports rose 16.4% YoY to 190,125 units while domestic volumes fell 2.3%; Middle East & Africa (+30% in Q3 FY26) and Latin America (+13%) drove growth and HMIL positions India as an export hub for Hyundai. No explicit China+1 framing found.

rural.evidence: Rural share of domestic sales rose to 23.6% in Q2 FY26, over 24% in Q3 and a record ~25% in Q4 FY26 (25.9% in Q1 FY27); management targets ~30% in 3-4 years. Full-year FY26 rural share not found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Proxy: FY26 export volume share (190,125 of 775,031 units, ~24.5%). The AR 2025-26 'FY26 at a glance' revenue split appears to show roughly 22% export / 78% domestic for FY26 but the extracted text was garbled, so the volume share is used. Hedging policy not found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Hyundai Motor India was among the 20 Champion OEMs approved under the Auto PLI scheme (Feb 2022); no disbursement to HMIL reported in coverage through Nov 2025. Upcoming local EV designed to be PLI-compliant; Creta Electric certification awaited.

china_plus_one.evidence: Management sized FY26 exports at ~US$80-85mn (~40% growth), CDM/OEM-only, with a US foray progressing despite tariffs and supplies to Europe started in FY26; targets ~US$100mn incremental exports by FY28. No explicit China+1 attribution found.

govt_capex.evidence: Electro-Mechanical Projects & Commercial AC segment was Rs 6,762.8 cr (~54.5% of FY26 revenue) with EMP order book ~Rs 4,664 cr at Mar-26; railway electrification/metro and infrastructure inflows were described as subdued, with the company prioritising data centres (~Rs 1,000 cr FY26 revenue), factories and hospitals. No government-order share disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Management/commentary flags volatility in commodity prices (including plastics) and exchange rates as margin risks in FY26; no share of crude-linked inputs disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Proxy: FY26 exports ~US$80-85mn vs FY26 revenue Rs 12,402 cr implies ~6% (own calculation). Currency volatility flagged as a margin risk; hedging policy not found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Subsidiary Blue Star Climatech was approved under the PLI scheme for white goods (AC components) for its Sri City plant, expected to receive ~Rs 73 cr over five years from FY2024 on ~Rs 153 cr eligible plant & machinery investment.

china_plus_one.evidence: IT services exporter (~90% overseas revenue); FY26 USD revenue grew 17.4% to $1,654.4mn with North America +17.2%, Europe +26.7%, RoW +27.5%. No supply-chain diversification angle.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Rolling forward-contract hedge book: ~US$440mn (Jun-25), US$475mn at Rs 87.8 (Sep-25), ~US$500mn at ~Rs 90.70 (Mar-26), US$500mn at Rs 93.30 (Jun-26).
inr_exposure.evidence: Proxy: overseas revenue share. Geographic split used is Q1 FY27 (NA 79.1%, Europe 8.5%, India 9.8%, RoW 2.6%) from a secondary summary as the FY26 full-year split was not found; FY26 growth rates by region imply a similar mix.

china_plus_one.evidence: Exports ~75% of FY26 revenue (Rs 2,120 cr) across 90+ countries; after US tariffs cut PPF share from 31% to 25%, the company pushed Middle East (30-40% growth expected) and Europe (~20%). Also benefits from DGTR anti-dumping recommendation on Chinese TPU PPF imports, but no explicit China+1 export narrative.

crude_exposure.evidence: Films made from PTA/MEG -> PET chips (crude derivatives); management says crude-linked raw material swings affect only a small part of product cost given high value addition in coatings/adhesives. No % disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Proxy: FY26 export share ~75% (guided to stay >70% in FY27+). US is the key PPF market (tariffs of up to 50% partly absorbed in FY26, cut to 10% in Feb 2026), but US share not disclosed. Hedging policy not found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Exports ~8-8.5% of revenue (FY25 standalone export sales Rs 1,405 cr of Rs 16,932 cr product sales); export demand described as stable with new lines like NOx sensors growing. No diversification narrative.

rural.evidence: Tractor demand was cited as a driver of Mobility/Powertrain growth in FY25; FY26 growth led by Power Solutions and two-wheelers. No rural share disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Proxy: export share ~8% (FY25 standalone 8.3% of product sales; management cites 8-8.5%). FY26 export figure and hedging policy not found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Bosch Limited is listed among approved Component Champion applicants under the Auto PLI scheme (82 approved as of 30 Nov 2025); FY26 payout reports name sister entity Bosch Automotive Electronics India, not Bosch Ltd.

china_plus_one.evidence: Domestic diagnostics business; small international labs in Nepal and Bangladesh, plus a Dubai subsidiary approved in FY26 for overseas acquisitions. No export or China+1 angle.

rural.evidence: Tier-3-plus towns were reported at 39% of FY26 revenue (about Rs 1,090 cr), up from 34% in FY23. This is a semi-urban/small-town proxy, not strictly rural. FY26 regional split: Delhi NCR 31%, UP/UK 19%, Rest of North 13%, East 15%, West 14%, South 6%, Others 2% (secondary summary).

rate_sensitive.evidence: Largely debt-free diagnostics company; no floating-rate borrowing exposure disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Proxy: international operations (Nepal, Bangladesh) reported at under 2% of revenue in FY25, consistent with the 'Others 2%' bucket in the FY26 regional split. No hedging policy found.

china_plus_one.evidence: LNG import and regasification business serving the Indian market; no export business.

govt_capex.evidence: Promoted by PSU oil and gas companies (GAIL, IOC, BPCL, ONGC), which are also major offtakers and capacity users. No revenue percentage was found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Main fixed-charge liabilities are USD-denominated tanker lease liabilities, which are an FX rather than a floating-rate exposure. No floating-rate debt share was found.

crude_exposure.evidence: LNG purchase cost (cost of materials consumed) was about Rs 37,120 cr against standalone revenue of Rs 43,495 cr in FY26, roughly 85% of revenue. The long-term Qatar contract (about 7.5-8.5 mtpa) is priced at about a 12-12.67% slope to Brent, so LNG cost is crude-linked, but it is largely passed through to offtakers.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Takes no open position on foreign-currency loans and hedges forex fluctuations. Its accounting policies list forward contracts, cross-currency and interest-rate swaps, and options (secondary summary of the FY24 annual report).
inr_exposure.evidence: LNG is bought in USD and sold on a pass-through basis. FX losses arise mainly from restating USD tanker lease liabilities (e.g. Rs 258 cr exchange loss in FY23). No USD revenue share was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Predominantly domestic spirits business (FY26 net sales Rs 12,467 cr, more than 90% Prestige & Above). The India-UK FTA concluded in FY26 is flagged as a tailwind through lower Scotch import duties, an import angle rather than an export one. No export share was found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key inputs are ENA/grain/molasses and glass; management cited benign commodity inflation in FY26. No crude-derivative share was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Strong export momentum: Europe crossed EUR 1 bn in FY26 (Q4 +30% YoY to Rs 2,795 cr) and Growth Markets grew 10% to Rs 3,499 cr. Backward integration into Pen-G at Kakinada reduces dependence on Chinese KSMs. Sector China+1 commentary exists, but no company-specific growth was attributed to China+1. The company also runs its own China OSD plant supplying Europe.

inr_exposure.evidence: Proxy: US formulations were 40% of consolidated revenue in Q4 FY26 (43% of standalone FY26 revenue per the directors' report); Europe (EUR) is another ~30%. Q4 FY26 included a Rs 48 cr forex loss. Hedging policy not found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Step-down subsidiary Lyfius Pharma's 15,000 MT Penicillin-G plant at Kakinada was approved under the bulk-drug PLI scheme (about Rs 2,400-2,500 cr investment) and inaugurated in Oct 2024. Production restarted on 29 Jun 2025 after pollution-board consent. No PLI incentive or revenue figure was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Mumbai-focused real estate developer; FY26 revenue was Rs 5,811 cr real estate and Rs 198 cr hospitality, all in India.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Borrowings fell about 15% to Rs 2,816 cr at Mar-2026 from about Rs 3,300 cr, on lower NCDs; D/E 0.16 vs 0.21 and cash about Rs 1,697 cr. Housing demand is rate-sensitive and brokers flag rising rates as a key risk. The fixed/floating split was not found.
